His youngest son Kim Jong-un (born 1983 or 1984) assumed power within days as Supreme Leader. He was educated in Switzerland. Within his first years, he had his uncle Jang Song-thaek executed (December 2013) and his half-brother Kim Jong-nam assassinated with VX nerve agent (February 2017). What is his nuclear program status?
answer: Successful nuclear weapons development — six tests by 2017, including a hydrogen bomb; intercontinental ballistic missiles (Hwasong-14, Hwasong-15) demonstrated by 2017
choices: Successful nuclear weapons development — six tests by 2017, including a hydrogen bomb; intercontinental ballistic missiles (Hwasong-14, Hwasong-15) demonstrated by 2017
Nuclear program rolled back through diplomacy — Trump's 2018-2019 summits with Kim produced verifiable denuclearization agreements that have continued
Limited nuclear capability without effective delivery systems — North Korean technology has been hyped but technically inferior to Western and Russian assessments
Nuclear program transferred to civilian use — North Korean reactors have been redirected to power generation under international agreement
context: Kim Jong-un's nuclear and missile programs accelerated through his decade in power. Trump's 2018-2019 summits with Kim produced no verifiable agreements. Kim Yo-jong (Kim Jong-un's sister) has emerged as a political figure. North Korea remains in pariah status internationally. About 100,000 political prisoners remain in concentration camps. The regime survives despite international sanctions and economic isolation.

question: From late 2019 through 2023, the COVID-19 pandemic killed about 7 million people directly (true figure may exceed 20 million counting excess deaths). The SARS-CoV-2 virus was first identified in Wuhan, China. By March 11, 2020, the WHO had declared a pandemic. Governments imposed unprecedented restrictions. Vaccines were developed in record time (December 2020). What is the pandemic's significance?
answer: First major global pandemic in a century; accelerated remote work, telemedicine, and digital transformation; revealed weaknesses in international cooperation; political polarization deepened
choices: First major global pandemic in a century; accelerated remote work, telemedicine, and digital transformation; revealed weaknesses in international cooperation; political polarization deepened
Manageable health crisis comparable to seasonal flu — the response was disproportionate to the actual mortality threat
Demonstration of public health system effectiveness — the response prevented far worse outcomes through coordinated international action
Catastrophic policy failure — government responses caused more harm than the disease itself through economic and social disruption
context: About 7 million confirmed deaths; excess mortality estimates range from 15-30 million. The vaccines (Pfizer-BioNTech, Moderna, AstraZeneca, Johnson & Johnson, others) were developed in record time. The pandemic's economic, political, social, and psychological consequences continue to shape global politics in the 2020s. The 'lab leak' theory of the virus's origins remains contested. Long COVID affects millions.

question: On November 4, 2008, in the midst of the global financial crisis, Barack Obama (Democrat) defeated John McCain (Republican) to become the first African-American President of the United States. He carried 28 states and 365 electoral votes. He took office January 20, 2009. About 1.8 million attended his inauguration. He served two terms (2009-2017). His major achievements included Affordable Care Act (2010) and the killing of bin Laden (2011). What was the broader significance?

His legacy includes both policy achievements and the political polarization that produced the Trump phenomenon.

question: From January 25 to February 11, 2011, mass protests in Cairo's Tahrir Square and across Egypt forced the resignation of President Hosni Mubarak, who had ruled since 1981. Morsi died in court in June 2019. Egyptian human rights situation has worsened. Mubarak died in 2020 after his release from custody. Egypt has emerged as a major regional power but under increasingly authoritarian government.

question: On November 4, 2017, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) — son of King Salman — initiated a sweeping anti-corruption campaign that detained about 200 Saudi princes, ministers, and businessmen at Riyadh's Ritz-Carlton hotel. question: On August 24, 1991, after the failed Moscow coup against Gorbachev (August 19-22), the Verkhovna Rada (Ukrainian parliament) declared Ukrainian independence from the Soviet Union. The 2022 Russian invasion has been the largest European war since WWII. About 500,000 casualties by 2024.

question: From October 16 to 19, 1813, the Sixth Coalition's combined armies of 365,000 Russians, Prussians, Austrians, and Swedes under multiple commanders surrounded and crushed Napoleon's 195,000-man French army around a Saxon city. question: On October 25, 1854, during the Crimean War, a confused order misinterpreted by British Cavalry Division commanders led the Light Brigade of 670 men under Major General the Earl of Cardigan in a frontal charge against Russian artillery at the head of a valley. About 110 men were killed and 130 wounded. The charge was witnessed by French Marshal Pierre Bosquet who reportedly remarked what?

context: Tennyson's poem 'The Charge of the Light Brigade' (1854) made the disaster a legend. The order originated with Lord Raglan, was misinterpreted by Lord Lucan, and was carried out by Lord Cardigan. The Crimean War (1853-1856) ended Russia's role as Europe's dominant land power and was the first war reported by professional war correspondents.

question: After Actium on September 2, 31 BC, Octavian invaded Egypt the next year. Antony fell on his own sword (a slow death; he was carried to Cleopatra to die in her arms). Cleopatra, captured and held by Octavian, killed herself a few days later — by tradition with an asp's bite, more likely poison. What political shift did the conquest of Egypt mark for Rome?
